chunks: Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him say: “There is no servant who gives preference over hajj to a need from the needs of this world, except that he will look upon those who have shaved their heads having already departed before that need is fulfilled for him.”

key_terms.الْحَجِّ: the pilgrimage to the Sacred House, treated here as a duty not to be postponed for worldly concerns
key_terms.الْمُحَلِّقِينَ: those who have shaved their heads after completing the pilgrimage rites
key_terms.حَوَائِجِ الدُّنْيَا: the needs and concerns of worldly life

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about delaying hajj for worldly needs?
ai.summary: This hadith warns against preferring worldly concerns over performing hajj. It emphasizes that delaying this act of worship for worldly needs brings regret, as others complete the pilgrimage before one's worldly objective is even fulfilled.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2863 - Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja'far (as), who said:

"I heard him say: 'No servant gives preference to a worldly need over performing Hajj except that he will see the pilgrims, having completed their rituals and shaved their heads, return before his need is fulfilled.'"
